title: Braun ET66 calculator, 1987
lede: The pocket calculator by Dieter Rams and Dietrich Lubs that inspired the iPhone’s Calculator app.
summary: A black calculator with round keys, the physical model for the iOS Calculator. Braun, 1987.

creator.name: Dieter Rams and Dietrich Lubs for Braun AG

evidence.note: Based on the Powerhouse Collection record 2012/33/1 and Cult of Mac (2013). The record’s image was not inspected.

styles.note: Not an example of the style: the physical object that an interface imitated. It shows that the style also borrowed from restrained modern products, not only from leather and wood.
Partial fit: a later Braun product by Rams and Lubs that keeps the plain housing and round keys of the product core, but in black plastic and outside the era.

context: Powerhouse Collection: Braun ET66 calculator, made 1987, designed by Dieter Rams and Dietrich Lubs, manufactured by Braun AG and made in Hong Kong; “black plastic, including a case, with round numeric and function keys.” [Powerhouse, 2012/33/1](https://collection.powerhouse.com.au/object/428164).

Cult of Mac (John Brownlee, 2 May 2013): “the Braun ET66 pocket calculator, first released in 1987 … inspired iOS’s own calculator app.” [Cult of Mac](https://www.cultofmac.com/news/buy-a-replica-of-the-classic-braun-calculator-that-inspired-ioss-calculator-app).
interpretation: An interface can imitate an object that is itself plain. The iOS calculator kept the ET66’s round-key layout and color accents, not a material texture.

rights.statement: Design by living and recent designers; the museum states that image copyright is held by the Powerhouse. No image is stored here.
